title: Beyond Thinking: Imagining in 360$^\circ$ for Humanoid Visual Search
claim: Separating imagination of unseen spatial layout from action selection lets an agent find targets in fewer, better-guided steps.
layout: 3 columns left-to-right, Actor on top, Imaginator below, unfolded scenes at bottom
description: A three-step walkthrough of a search episode for the query 'Q: Locate the timetable.' The top row shows camera views from a train station at three timesteps. Each has a camera coordinate label and a speech bubble with the Actor's command: Rotate(-150,10), Rotate(-20,10), then Submit(10,20). A cartoon Actor robot stands on a conveyor belt. Below it, a cartoon Imaginator robot sits in a thought cloud. The cloud lists [Observed] and [Imagined] objects with coordinates, such as Person, Staircase and Timetable, and arrows pass these suggestions up to the Actor. At the bottom left, a sphere marks the 360° environment. Three unfolded panoramic scenes follow it, with pins and green or purple object labels. Imagined objects appear in purple and confirmed objects in green. The eye goes first to the robots and the top camera frames.
caption: Imagining in 360◦: We propose a decoupled architecture for Humanoid Visual Search (HVS). The Imaginator explicitly models the 360◦environment by predicting the semantic layout of both observed and unseen regions, which provides the downstream Actor with a sampled distribution of spatial priors as suggestions. This explicit imagination empowers the agent to reorient its head more efficiently, hedging against spatial uncertainty in complex, in-the-wild environments.
abstract: Humanoid Visual Search (HVS) requires agents to actively explore immersive 360$^\circ$ environments. While prior methods treat this as a monolithic task relying on cumulative, multi-turn Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, they impose heavy cognitive burdens and require expensive trajectory-level annotations. In this paper, we propose Imagining in 360$^\circ$, a novel framework that decouples the exploration process into a specialized Imaginator and an Actor. The Imaginator functions as a probabilistic predictor of spatial priors; instead of maintaining a cumulative reasoning chain, it infers the semantic layout of both observed and unobserved regions in a single step. By sampling multiple hypotheses within this semantic space, we provide the Actor with a distribution of effective spatial information, offering robust guidance that hedges against uncertainty during active search. This decoupled architecture significantly lowers data engineering costs by eliminating the need for full-trajectory CoT annotations, enabling the generation of over 1.96 million curated training samples. Extensive experiments demonstrate that explicitly modeling semantic spatial priors drastically improves search efficiency and success rates in complex, in-the-wild environments.
